name: NVIDIA PTX ABI

dataModel.executionModel: SIMT — single instruction, multiple threads grouped in warps

stack.notes: PTX kernels do not use a CPU call stack. Per-thread private state uses .local memory (spills, alloca). Shared data uses .shared. Kernel parameters are declared in .param space and loaded by the generated prologue. The CUDA driver JIT-compiles PTX to SASS for the specific SM.

layout.label: Global Memory (.global)
layout.description: Device-visible arrays and pointer arguments. 64-bit generic addressing via ld/st.global or cvta.to.global.

layout.label: Parameter Space (.param)
layout.description: Kernel formal parameters and launch-bound values. .param .u64 for pointers; .param .align N .b8 arrays for structs.

layout.label: Shared Memory (.shared)
layout.description: Block-scoped shared memory (__shared__). Fast on-chip storage shared by all threads in a thread block.

layout.label: Local Memory (.local)
layout.description: Per-thread private memory for register spills and large stack frames. High latency compared to registers.

layout.label: Registers (.reg)
layout.description: Per-thread predicate (.pred), integer (.b32/.b64), and floating (.f32/.f64) registers. Register count limits occupancy.

variadicRules.notes: CUDA __global__ kernels have fixed signatures. Device-side function calls use .param passing for arguments per PTX ABI for device functions.

simple.title: Vector add kernel (CUDA → PTX)
simple.llvmIR:
define ptx_kernel void @vector_add(
    ptr addrspace(1) nocapture readonly %a,
    ptr addrspace(1) nocapture readonly %b,
    ptr addrspace(1) nocapture writeonly %c,
    i32 %n) #0 {
entry:
  ; NVPTX lowers to PTX with .param and special registers
  ret void
}
simple.notes: Parameters live in .param space and are loaded with ld.param. Thread index uses %tid/%ctaid/%ntid specials. Predicated branches (@%p1) handle the bounds check without CPU-style call stack.

complex.title: Shared memory tile
complex.notes: .shared is block-scoped. bar.sync is the block barrier — analogous to __syncthreads().

warp.title: Warp shuffle reduction
warp.notes: PTX exposes warp collective ops explicitly. Hardware executes 32 threads in lockstep per warp; divergence is handled via predication and reconvergence.

why.question: Why .param space instead of passing arguments in registers like CPU ABIs?
why.answer: Kernel launches are driven by the CUDA driver with varying parameter lists and sizes. .param gives a stable, documented layout the driver and JIT can populate without re-specializing the shader. The PTX prologue loads params into .reg files — similar in spirit to AMDGPU kernarg → SGPR loads.

why.question: Why SIMT with 32-thread warps?
why.answer: NVIDIA hardware schedules warps as the atomic execution unit — one program counter per warp, 32 lanes. SIMT lets programmers write thread-oriented code while hardware executes warp-oriented instructions. The warp size (32) is fixed across generations for binary and performance model consistency.

why.question: Why separate .shared, .local, and .global address spaces?
why.answer: Each space maps to different hardware with different latency, scope, and capacity. Explicit spaces let the compiler place data optimally: registers first, then shared, then local spills, with global for bulk data. LLVM NVPTX encodes these as address spaces 1–5 in IR.

why.question: Why predicate registers (.pred)?
why.answer: GPUs lack traditional branch prediction for divergent control flow. Predicated execution and @%p guarded instructions let both paths execute selectively without serializing the entire warp in many cases. PTX makes predicates first-class.
